L0: A procedure of replacing the underlying model partway through an already-running task, done to see whether the work can continue without disruption.
L1: A procedure of replacing the underlying model partway through an already-running task, done to see whether the work can continue without disruption. Concretely, the model driving a session is swapped to a newer or different release while the task is still in progress, with files already edited and earlier decisions already recorded in the running transcript. It is done either because a model change is forced mid-run (such as a vendor deprecation notice) or because the change is deliberately triggered mid-task, for example during a partial refactor.
L2: A procedure of replacing the underlying model partway through an already-running task, done to see whether the work continues cleanly. The model driving a session is swapped to a newer or different release while files are already edited and earlier decisions are recorded in the transcript; it applies when the change is forced mid-run (such as a vendor deprecation notice) or deliberately triggered mid-task, like a live refactor with several files modified and tests partly passing. What is measured is whether the continuation respects the existing file structure, prior naming decisions, and the existing diff, rather than discarding correct work, rewriting already-correct files, or re-reading the whole repository from scratch. It is scored as a coherent-continuation rate (for example 84%, up from 71%): the share of runs that pick up the thread without contradicting prior work. Outputs must be graded by more than one pass, since a single grader pass is not trusted after a mid-run change and repeated grading of identical content can return differing verdicts; continuation improves when file-edit history is explicitly preserved across the swap rather than left for the new model to infer.
